title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 21-23): Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'topological 1-forms' combinatorially. The data are a set L of 'lieux' (loci) and a set S ⊂ P(L) of 'segments'. Each segment I has a 2-element boundary ∂I ∈ P_2(I). The data satisfy axioms F1-F6, which include a 'recollement' (gluing) axiom and an axiom F6 on branches. A model is called a 'réseau' (network). Loci split into regular loci L_r (multiplicity 2) and singular/critical loci (nodes). Edges are the connected components of L_r minus the nodes. A network is 'réduit' if every segment equals its boundary (card I = 2), equivalently L_r = ∅.

This page, part 1. A discrete network structure on L amounts to giving a subset S ⊂ P_2(L). All segments are 2-element sets and there are no regular loci. The axioms F1-F6, which concern regular points, interiors and gluing, become vacuous. So a discrete/reduced network is the same thing as a 'reduced graph', i.e. a simple graph: no loops, no multiple edges, edges identified with 2-element vertex sets.

Part 2 (programme). He wants to classify regular connected non-empty networks (L_r = L, '0-connexe'). These are the combinatorial analogue of connected 1-manifolds: one expects only the 'line' and the 'circle' types. A marginal note seems to say that the case analysis should work for arbitrary networks, provided only that y is regular.

The tool is a local lemma on two 'convergent' segments I (from x to y) and J (from y to z). They meet at a regular locus y ∈ ∂I ∩ ∂J and have different branches there, br_y(I) ≠ br_y(J).
- Case I: I ∩ J = {y}. The gluing axiom gives a unique K ∈ S with K ⊃ I ∪ J and ∂K = {x,z}, and I = K_{xy}, J = K_{yz} (sub-segments). This is 'well understood'.
- Case II: I ∩ J ≠ {y}, with sub-cases:
  - (a) x = z: the two arcs close up into a circle (the drawn ellipse).
  - (b) there is t ∈ I ∩ J with t ≠ y.

The next page continues. When ∂I = ∂J and the branches differ at y, F6 forces the branches to differ at x too, and then I ∩ J = {x,y}. This is the circle case, the key step toward 'line or circle'.
errors: No real error. One implicit limitation: since segments are subsets of L, a discrete network gives only simple graphs. Multigraphs, loops and parallel edges cannot be encoded, hence 'graphe réduit'. Later (p.23) the circle made of two segments with the same boundary needs non-reduced segments, consistent with this.
The page is a draft: Case II is reorganized (struck-through text, notation changed on the next page). The case split is not complete on this page.

ideas.what: Discrete (reduced) networks are exactly simple graphs: a network structure with all segments of cardinality 2 is just a subset of P_2(L); the axioms become vacuous.
ideas.modern_name: simple graph as a 1-dimensional combinatorial space / reduced 1-complex

ideas.what: Local gluing lemma: two segments meeting only at a regular point with distinct branches glue to a unique larger segment containing them as sub-segments.
ideas.modern_name: concatenation of arcs in a 1-manifold; betweenness/interval-space axiomatics
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (characterization of arcs/1-manifolds; Hilbert-style order axioms)

ideas.what: Programme to classify connected regular networks (axiomatic 1-manifolds) via case analysis of convergent segments, leading to the line/circle dichotomy.
ideas.modern_name: classification of connected 1-manifolds in a synthetic/tame setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical topology; tame-topology analogues (o-minimal structures, van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this axiomatics is not there

missed.claim: This is part of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatic 'géométrie des formes': a combinatorial, point-set axiomatization of 1-dimensional shapes by segments with boundaries and branches. Discrete models recover simple graphs and regular ones are meant to give line/circle. The page itself is routine, but the framework as a whole is not in the literature.
missed.quote: La donnée d'une structure de réseau discret sur L revient à celle d'une partie S de P_2(L) [les axiomes F1) à F6) sont vides!] donc à une structure de graphe réduit.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's attempt at a synthetic tame topology unifying graphs (cf. dessins/maps) and topological 1-manifolds. This is of historical interest for tame-topology programmes; the mathematics on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary observations (discrete networks = simple graphs; gluing of arcs at a regular point) within an unpublished axiomatic framework. Historically interesting, but the content is routine.
transcription_corrections: '[-Lemme-]' is indeed struck out before 'On va étudier'.
Line before 'avec br_y(I)≠br_y(J)' looks like 'x∈∂I∩∂J' in the hand, but y∈∂I∩∂J is meant; 'bry' should be read br_y (branch at y), consistent with 'bor_y' on p.23.
Margin reading uncertain: possibly 'Rq: quelconques ... en y réguliers', i.e. a remark that only regularity at y is needed.
